reasoning.statement: mountControl creates and assigns a controlState before entering the kind switch.

The supported MenuButton branch invokes mountMenuButton; that helper assigns its menuState before registering any event callbacks (menu_button.go:80). Neither state pointer is subsequently cleared on this route.
The one production r.control=nil assignment is only the mountControl default for unsupported kinds, which returns without a managed widget/menu callback. It cannot be reached by a mounted MenuButton.
postControl is the gateway for all cited queued closures. It wraps them in PostWindow and calls fn only if the captured record is not retired.
disposeControl first sets retired=true, then retires popup/native resources; it leaves controlState/menuState pointers intact. Already admitted owner work therefore skips the inner closure.
A kind change is incompatible (compatible at line237), so reconciliation mounts a distinct new record. It does not repurpose the old menu record into the unsupported branch.
PostWindow also skips its admitted callback when the captured window lifetime is canceled.

conclusion: The provider scenario assumes unmount clears mounted menu control/menu pointers. Actual supported routing preserves those pointers and revokes via retired/window lifetime. No reachable production path establishes the proposed nil dereference, so no defensive source change or new test is warranted.
